questions.question_text: In an electrical grid network diagram where vertices represent power substations and edges represent transmission lines, what does a weight of $18\text{ MW}$ assigned to edge $XY$ represent?

options.text: The power transmission capacity or energy loss along the power line between substations $X$ and $Y$
The total electrical power generated by substation $X$ alone
options.why: Confused the weight on a connecting edge with the power output of a single vertex.

options.text: The geographic distance in kilometres between substations $X$ and $Y$
options.why: Ignored the unit megawatts (MW) which represents electrical power rather than distance.

options.text: The number of high-voltage transformers installed at substation $Y$
options.why: Mistook the edge transmission rating for an equipment count inside a single substation.

questions.solution_text:
In electrical grid networks, vertices represent substations and edges represent transmission lines.
Edge weights in megawatts ($\text{MW}$) quantify the electrical power transmission capacity or power loss along the connecting line.
A weight of $18\text{ MW}$ on edge $XY$ represents the power transmission capacity or energy loss along the power line between substations $X$ and $Y$.

questions.question_text:
A directed traffic network has valid paths from Start ($S$) to Exit ($T$):
Path 1: $S\to A\to T$ with weight $23$
Path 2: $S\to B\to T$ with weight $28$
Path 3: $S\to A\to B\to T$ with weights $SA=14, AB=9, BT=12$
What is the weight of the **longest** valid directed path from $S$ to $T$?

options.why: Selected Path 2 without evaluating the multi-step Path 3.
Selected the shortest path instead of the longest path.
Subtracted $3$ from Path 3 due to an addition error ($14 + 9 + 12 = 35$).

questions.solution_text:
$S\to A\to T = 23$
$S\to B\to T = 28$
$S\to A\to B\to T = 14 + 9 + 12$
$= 35$
Longest valid path: $S\to A\to B\to T$, weight: $35$
